headline: Approved $64,600 for Lake Street fire station roof and $42,536 for Firewall Street bridge design; Felton Street zoning change tabled.
summary: Four funding requests were approved, including $6,760 for culvert work and $40,000 for professional services. Resolutions backing the Salvation Army and recognizing Small Business Saturday were approved, while two Kevin M. Ritzy Award resolutions were tabled. The council then went into executive session on a possible purchase at 14th through 16th Spring Street.
decisions: Tabled the mayor's request for executive session on 14th through 16th Spring Street.
Tabled the mayor's confidential communication on 14th through 16th Spring Street.
Approved the Salvation Army Red Kettle bell ringing resolution.
Approved the resolution recognizing Small Business Saturday, November 28, 2026.
Tabled the Kevin M. Ritzy Award resolution naming Joanne Raymond for 2025.
Tabled the Kevin M. Ritzy Award resolution naming Douglas Wabry for 2026.
Approved the suicide prevention awareness month resolution.
Approved $64,600 to replace the roof at the Lake Street fire station.
Approved $42,536 for the preliminary design of Firewall Street bridge repair.
Approved $6,760 for expanded work on the Chesterbrook Culvert at Beaver Street lining project.
Approved $40,000 for professional services by former school finance official Lillianne Winski.
Gave first reading to the zoning amendment for 181 through 185 Felton Street.
Tabled the zoning amendment for 181 through 185 Felton Street.
Approved the secondhand dealers license at 1275 Main Street.
Approved the secondhand dealers license at 550 Moody Street.
Approved seven extended hours and license renewals together, agenda items 3 to 9.
Approved going into executive session on 14th through 16th Spring Street, with 13 in favor.
discussion: Salvation Army bell ringing: Speakers described the Salvation Army's services, including 24,000 meals and 850 backpacks. The council's bell ringing is set for Friday, December 4, at Market Basket.
Small business resolution: Speakers said local businesses give back through donations and volunteer time, and they urged residents to shop locally.
Kevin M. Ritzy Award: The award presentations were tabled so they can be scheduled at a time that works for each recipient.
14th through 16th Spring Street: It was said that an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on the city's negotiating position.
Veterans Day ceremony: Councilors announced a public ceremony on Wednesday, November 11, at the Circle of Remembrance, starting at 11 a.m.
